_what_this_is: What is ACTUALLY in the Stripe dashboard, as of the dates below: the products, their prices, and the coupons. It is not a plan and it is not generated from this repository's data — it is the other side of a reconciliation, so the two can be compared and a drift can be caught. The build emits what the offers imply; this file says what exists; a check puts them side by side.
_provenance: Product ids, names and descriptions from the dashboard's own CSV export, committed verbatim at data/admin/stripe-products.csv. The amounts are not in that export and were read off the product list in the dashboard on the same day. That is a weaker source than the CSV and it is said here rather than blurred — the amounts are the half a person typed.
_the_split_is_theirs_and_it_is_better: The two upper levels are two products each, DEPOSIT and DELIVERY, summing to the full price — rather than one product plus a separate deposit price. A buyer who wants to pay in full adds both lines; a buyer who wants to start adds the deposit. The store had always said a fifth now and the rest on delivery, and this is that sentence as two rows rather than as a rule somebody has to apply.

_not_ours: One more product exists on the account and is deliberately not listed here: SG/Send Credits — Starter Pack, £5. It is a different product from a different part of the estate and this store neither sells it nor reconciles it.
_renamed: Level four was called 'Two sessions, and a professional signs it' here and 'ABP - Two sessions and a custom vault' in Stripe. The store followed the Stripe name on 16 September: it is the later decision and the better one, because it says what the buyer ends up holding rather than what happens to it. The professional signing it has not been dropped — it is on the level's own page, where it is a property of the thing rather than the name of it.
_the_key_is_a_description_not_a_lookup_k: Every price carries its code in the Stripe PRICE DESCRIPTION field — ABP-T1, ABP-T3-DEPOSIT and so on — because the dashboard's product view does not surface a lookup key and the description is what was available. It works for a person reading the dashboard. It is NOT the same thing as Price.lookup_key, which exists on the API and is the field a webhook would query a line item back to an offer by. That difference is a real one and it is written down here rather than found later by a handler that cannot tell which level was bought.
_prefix: ABP-, not the SG- this plan first proposed. The project lead's choice and the better one: the prefix names the product rather than the company.
_coupon_ids_are_not_printed_on_the_site: The ids below are in this repository because the reconciliation has to be able to point at a specific row. They are NOT rendered on any page. A coupon id is not the thing a buyer applies — what a buyer applies, or a link carries in prefilled_promo_code, is a PROMOTION CODE, and none of those exists yet. So publishing the id would most likely be harmless, and not publishing it costs nothing, and this store does not spend a maybe on a convenience. Confirm the promotion-code-versus-coupon-id behaviour against the dashboard before the first link goes out.
_the_gap_between_a_coupon_and_a_code: A coupon carries the percentage. A promotion code is the string a person is handed and is a separate object attached to a coupon. Three coupons exist; zero promotion codes do. The EIGHT strings in data/discounts.yml are the promotion codes to create (this note said seven until 17 September, which was right before DOORSOPEN was added and wrong afterwards). Seven of the eight map onto these three coupons. The eighth does not, and that is the next note.
_doorsopen_needs_a_coupon_of_its_own: DOORSOPEN is `levels: [pack, vault]` in data/discounts.yml, and that restriction CANNOT be expressed on a promotion code. A promotion code's restrictions are first_time_transaction and a minimum amount; scoping a discount to particular products is a property of the COUPON, through applies_to.products. So DOORSOPEN needs a fourth coupon — 100% off, applies_to the two level-one and level-two products — and must not be attached to the shared 100% coupon. Attached to the shared one it would take the whole of a level-four deposit off, which is exactly the outcome that record's own comment says must not be possible: what it gives away has to be a thing that costs nobody a day. Confirm the behaviour in the dashboard before the code is handed to anybody.
_the_reference_is_the_only_thing_that_tr: The store appends client_reference_id to a payment link and nothing else but prefilled_promo_code. It does not send an amount: a payment link carries its own price and the store cannot set one in a URL, which is why the four links have to be created against the right products rather than against a total. The two upper levels' links are the DEPOSIT products, because pay_now_pct is 20 and the deposit is exactly a fifth; the DELIVERY halves are invoiced and have no link today.
